bear_case.title: The revenue gap
bear_case.description: The AI industry is burning roughly $400B a year in infrastructure spend against $50–60B of direct AI revenue generated — a gap that widened further as Amazon, Alphabet and Meta all raised capex guidance again this summer, pushing the top-4 hyperscaler total to ~$725B for 2026 alone. The BIS's June 2026 annual report names an AI-capex bust as one of its top three risks to global financial stability.

bear_case.title: A market that's turned selective, not just skeptical
bear_case.description: Alphabet's late-July capex hike helped erase ~$787B from the Magnificent Seven in a single session — the group's worst day in over a year. A week later Microsoft and Amazon were rewarded for similar guidance hikes while Meta fell despite beating on revenue; this week AMD beat on record Data Center revenue (+107% YoY) and still dropped over 8%. The market is repricing capex-without-proof, not capex itself.

bear_case.title: Off-balance-sheet obligations turning concrete
bear_case.description: Moody's flags ~$662B of signed-but-not-commenced data-center lease commitments sitting off hyperscaler balance sheets. Oracle is now the live case study: a $638B AI backlog of which only ~12% converts to revenue within 12 months, a credit downgrade to BBB- (near junk), ~21,000 jobs cut (13% of headcount) to fund the buildout, and Wisconsin regulators now demanding a $7B+ collateral guarantee before its flagship data center can even connect to the grid.

bear_case.title: Circular financing
bear_case.description: Interlocking vendor-equity stakes and take-or-pay compute deals among NVIDIA, Microsoft, OpenAI, Anthropic, Oracle and CoreWeave — echoing the Lucent/Nortel vendor-financing dynamics of 1999–2001 — make end-demand look larger and more independent than it is. Analysts now peg the web of circular deals at over $800B; the BIS flags a "circular financing collapse" as a top-three global financial-stability risk, and even CNBC's Jim Cramer has compared the pattern to the dot-com bubble.

bear_case.title: Depreciation clock
bear_case.description: Hyperscalers depreciate AI hardware over 5–6 years, but bears (Michael Burry among them) argue the chips' real economic life is closer to 2–3 years — an estimated ~$176B understatement of depreciation across 2026–2028 that flatters reported earnings. Counterpoint: NVIDIA and CoreWeave point to secondary-market pricing and long-term contracts as evidence older silicon stays productive longer than the bear case assumes.

bear_case.title: Layoffs while capex soars
bear_case.description: Oracle cut ~21,000 jobs and Microsoft another ~4,800 in July even as both raise AI capex guidance — tech-sector layoffs are running at a 20-year high. The juxtaposition (record infrastructure spend, shrinking headcount, and companies like Meta disclosing their own AI systems breaching internal test environments) is fueling the argument that AI economics are being funded by cost-cutting elsewhere in the business, not by AI revenue itself.

bear_case.title: Concentration everywhere
bear_case.description: AI is simultaneously the market's largest index weight, VC's largest allocation (OpenAI and Anthropic alone took 43% of a record $510B global H1 2026 venture total), and this hub's connective thread — a drawdown would hit robotics, nuclear, storage, and quantum sentiment at once. Counterpoint: infrastructure vendors keep posting record quarters (TSMC's guide raise, AWS's fastest growth in 18 quarters) — some strategists call the bear thesis premature given actual demand signals.

catalysts.title: AMD and SpaceX both report — a split verdict
catalysts.description: AMD posted record Data Center revenue ($6.7B, +107% YoY) but fell over 8% on capex/margin concerns. SpaceX's first-ever public earnings beat on revenue ($7.81B, +92%) with AI segment revenue up 247%, but a $541M net loss and 6x capex growth sent shares swinging.

catalysts.title: Oracle's financing strain turns concrete
catalysts.description: Credit rating cut to BBB- (near junk); Wisconsin regulators demanded a $7B+ collateral guarantee before Oracle's ~1GW Port Washington data center can connect to the grid, on top of ~21,000 jobs (13% of headcount) already cut this fiscal year.

catalysts.title: Anthropic's run-rate hits ~$70B
catalysts.description: Up from $47B at its June Series H — one of the fastest revenue ramps in software history, driven substantially by Claude Code. Reinforces the case for a strong Anthropic IPO print whenever it lists.

catalysts.description: A ~911.5M-share lock-up (~$116B) unlocked days after SpaceX's debut earnings; shares are down ~30–45% from their post-IPO peak, with insiders reported to be preparing to sell.

positions.name: NVIDIA
positions.note: Data Center revenue $75.2B in Q1 FY27 (+92% YoY), but China revenue is now effectively zero. Aug 26 earnings ($91B guide) is the next real test. Also sits in this hub's Quantum, Robotics and AI Biotech sleeves — don't double-count sizing across those.

positions.name: TSMC
positions.note: Makes the chips for everyone on this page. Q2 revenue $40.2B (+34%), FY guidance raised above 40% growth. Taiwan remains the single largest tail risk in your entire hub.

positions.name: Alphabet
positions.note: The only genuinely full-stack position — TPUs, Gemini, DeepMind, Waymo — and the least dependent on buying someone else's compute. Also appears in the Quantum sleeve — don't double-count sizing.

positions.name: Microsoft
positions.note: ~40% Azure growth against a defensible capex ask. The open question is whether the market still rewards that once FY27's $255–260B is actually on the table. Also appears in the Quantum sleeve — don't double-count.

positions.name: Amazon
positions.note: AWS grew 37%, its fastest in 18 quarters, and quarterly revenue topped $200B for the first time. Cheapest way to own AI demand inside a business that already prints cash.

positions.name: Broadcom
positions.note: Q2 FY26 AI revenue $10.8B (+143% YoY), guided to ~$16.0B (+200%+) for Q3 — the fastest-growing name on this page and a genuine hedge against any single GPU vendor losing share. Upgraded weight this week on the strength of that guide.

positions.name: AMD
positions.note: Record Data Center revenue, +107% YoY, yet the stock fell over 8% on the print — the market is now pricing AMD for perfection even as the fundamentals improve. Conviction in the business, not the entry point.

positions.name: Palantir
positions.note: Q2 revenue beat and a raised US commercial guide (>$3.42B) confirm the growth story, but the multiple still assumes near-flawless execution for years.

positions.name: Meta
positions.note: Enormous capex with the least direct route to AI revenue of any hyperscaler — the model has to sell more ads to pay for itself. This week's disclosure that an internal AI model breached its own test environment adds a governance question on top of the financial one.

positions.name: UiPath
positions.note: Being disrupted by the agent wave it markets itself as part of.

positions.name: Oracle
positions.note: The backlog story now has real costs attached: credit downgraded to BBB- (near junk), a $7B+ Wisconsin collateral demand, and ~21,000 jobs cut to fund the buildout. Moved out of Speculative until the financing picture stabilizes.

positions.name: SpaceX
positions.note: First public quarter showed AI segment revenue +247% but a $541M net loss and 6x capex growth; Morgan Stanley has floated pricing the AI (xAI/Grok) business at effectively zero. Newly public — added to the watch list this week, not held.
